findings.text: non-blocking: _require_private_package now calls require_private_package with its default set_private=True, so a registry that reports public but accepts the private set no longer refuses the push; the done_when's literal case (registry faked to report public, push exits nonzero) now holds only for a package that stays public, and tests/cli/test_graph_push_private_package.py was renamed to say so. This is a deliberate and documented improvement (content already uploaded stops being publicly readable), but a coordinator reconciling the record against the declared done_when should see the case changed.

non-blocking: the assertion 'private (registry-reported)' in result.output cannot fail if the code echoes the requested visibility instead of the registry's report, because the fake returns the test-supplied after_set='private'; it is not independent of the value the test passed in. The exit-code, recorded-set and tag assertions beside it are independent and do carry the behaviour.

item_verdicts.diff: read the five-file increment a3812f9e..eb6b1c0d commit by commit; 9e252aa72 replaces the hand-rolled manifest reader with offsite.read_archive_manifest/GraphCensus (registry.py:554), makes _require_private_package set private before verifying (registry.py:566) and rewires the tests, and eb6b1c0dd updates the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks each push path to exit nonzero with no latest tag when the registry reports public; tests/cli/test_graph_push_private_package.py:242 now asserts refusal only for a package that stays public, :257 asserts a public-but-settable package continues, and the DD-only (:307) and manifestless (:415) cases are unchanged.
item_verdicts.goal: the source node's goal is that a facility-bearing graph push fails unless its registry package reads back private; the increment keeps the decision at iter_codex/cli/graph/registry.py:986 (local) and :878 (remote) and now sets private first at ghcr.py:796 before the read-back.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the reviewed manifest; it records commits a01663fba, a3812f9e, 9e252aa7 and eb6b1c0d, base arm 49 passed and after arm 61 passed (both EXIT=0 on disk) and a negative control at 1 failed/EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are iter_codex/cli/graph/registry.py, iter_codex/graph/ghcr.py, iter_codex/graph/remote.py, tests/cli, tests/graph and the evidence fragment; the increment touches only registry.py, the fragment and three tests/cli files, all inside that set.

justifications.durability: tests/cli/test_graph_push_private_package.py:257 reddens if the set is dropped and :283 reddens if an already-private package is written, so both directions of the new behaviour are guarded.
justifications.evidence: the manifest's gate runs the graph CLI suite on both arms and the on-disk logs end "61 passed"/"49 passed" with EXIT=0 and the negative control "1 failed"/EXIT=1, so the done_when measure is recorded rather than claimed.
justifications.fit: the additions follow the surrounding registry.py idiom and docstrings, and no added name, test name or comment carries a plan, version or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: registry.py:566 delegates to ghcr.require_private_package, which sets the package private and then fails unless the read-back is private, so the goal holds on the local (:986), remote (:878) and cycle (:463) paths.
justifications.reuse: registry.py:554 now extends iter_codex/graph/offsite.py:166 read_archive_manifest and :36 GraphCensus.from_manifest instead of re-implementing them, and the added ghcr helpers wrap the pre-existing require_private_package rather than duplicating it.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in a3812f9e..eb6b1c0d (registry.py, three tests/cli files and the one evidence fragment) is inside the declared write paths.
